xpts_breakdown.calibration_note: RAW uses the unmodified xpts.json priors (same inputs Sim Lab consumes) so the 3-way scoreboard compares like-for-like. I report both rather than hiding behind the inflated number - the calibrated 75.0 is my honest expectation.

differentials.case: The model's #2 asset overall and by a distance the best xPts-per-million pick in the entire GW2 pool (2.85 pts/m). Nobody at 5.6m in midfield is in the conversation - Xhaka is next best value at 1.15 pts/m. Even after applying the artifact cap he clears every mid I could buy for the money. This is the pick that has to land for me to beat the template.
Top-projecting forward in the whole dataset ahead of Haaland (6.43) at 9.5m less. Sub-radar third striker that lets me carry Haaland AND João Pedro without gutting the defence.

Intel's flagged sub-2% EO rank-chaser - GW1 direct free-kick match-winner, on set pieces, defensive-contribution points upside, soft Leeds run. Held on the bench as first midfield cover; promoted to the XI the moment his minutes are confirmed nailed.

captain_rationale: Haaland. Intel puts him at 69.3% owned / ~42% captained = ~111 EO and names him the outright template captain for GW2 at CRY (A). APEX captaincy protocol is explicit: nailed premium, never a GK, never a differential armband without a strong real-world signal. The raw cache would point the armband at Mendy (captain_xpts 32.84), but intel classifies that row as a corrupted artifact and rates captaining him a CRITICAL blowup risk - a 4.0m defender at ~0 EO. I own Haaland precisely so I can neutralise the single largest standing rank risk in the game this week, and captaining him caps my downside against the field. Vice is João Pedro: fdr 2, ~40 EO template core, and the highest-floor non-Haaland attacker I own (Gabriel was the alternative but ARS are the worst fixture tier at fdr 4).
strategy_notes: STRATEGY = top10k: mandated 3-4-3, safe-haven core plus a small number of calculated differentials. I own the three template assets that actually exist in the GW2 pool (Haaland, João Pedro, Gabriel) so I am never more than one captain-return away from the field, then take my rank swing in the cheap slots.

Structural bet: the GW2 model is bottom-heavy. HUL (fdr 2) and cheap value assets outrank almost every premium - Palmer projects 5.74 at 9.5m, Saka 4.03 at 9.5m, Isak 0.55 at 9.0m. I am deliberately underweight the premium mid/forward tier apart from Haaland and paying for a Hull goalkeeper + defender instead.

I capped my HUL exposure at 2 (Tzolakis + Mendy) rather than the legal 3. The raw model would have me stack Egan (11.18) and Giles (9.31) too, but intel explicitly warns those rows are inflated. Stacking a projection artifact three deep is how you lose a season, not win a week - so I took the fixture (fdr 2, cheap clean-sheet route) and left the artifact upside on the table.

Known cost of the mandated 3-4-3: Guéhi (7.31) sits on the bench while Xhaka (6.30) starts, because the shape caps me at three defenders. A 4-4-2 would score ~1.0 higher on the raw sheet, but 3-4-3 keeps three attacking returns live, which is the top10k playbook.
Club counts sit right on the limit at CHE 3 (Sánchez, Rogers, João Pedro). Any further CHE move requires a swap-out first - flagged for GW3 planning.

2.2m left in the bank, and that is on purpose. The premium tier projects so badly in this cache that there is nothing worth upgrading into; I would rather hold the liquidity for a GW3 reaction once real GW2 minutes data lands.
